accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal status of currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India and coins issued by the Government of India?
o: RBI notes are limited legal tender, whereas coins are unlimited legal tender
RBI notes are unlimited legal tender, whereas coins are limited legal tender
Both RBI notes and coins are limited legal tender
Neither RBI notes nor coins are legal tender unless specifically notified
accepted.x: Every RBI note is unlimited legal tender. Coins are limited legal tender.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between two closely related legal-tender categories.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to currency and coin issuance in India, consider the following statements:
1. RBI notes are signed by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.
2. The one-rupee note is signed by the Finance Secretary.
3. The Reserve Bank of India distributes coins as an agent of the Government of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Governor signs RBI notes, the one-rupee note is signed by the Finance Secretary, and the RBI distributes coins on behalf of the Government of India.
accepted.tq: Split the options by identifying the issuer, signatory and distributing agency.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Coinage Act, coins can be issued up to which of the following denominations?
accepted.x: The Coinage Act permits coins to be issued up to ₹1,000.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory ceiling rather than confusing it with the highest banknote denomination.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Before the introduction of the Minimum Reserve System, the Reserve Bank of India followed which system of currency backing?
accepted.x: Until 1956, currency issuance was backed under the proportional reserve system.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact technical term used for the earlier reserve arrangement.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the proportional reserve system followed before 1956, the reserve backing was prescribed in the proportion of:
accepted.x: The proportional reserve system required backing in the proportion of two-fifths gold and three-fifths sterling.
accepted.tq: Use the exact fraction pair and reject the reversed proportion.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Minimum Reserve System:
1. It replaced the proportional reserve system after 1956.
2. It requires a minimum reserve of ₹200 crore.
3. The gold component of the minimum reserve is ₹115 crore.
4. Once the minimum reserve is maintained, the RBI can issue currency without a statutory quantitative limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the Minimum Reserve System and its reserve composition of ₹200 crore, including ₹115 crore in gold.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical component and the consequence of maintaining the minimum reserve.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The highest denomination of currency note permitted under Section 24 of the Reserve Bank of India Act is:
accepted.x: Section 24 of the RBI Act permits a highest denomination of ₹10,000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory maximum from denominations currently in circulation.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the ₹10,000 note in chronological order:
A. Reintroduction of the ₹10,000 note
B. First introduction of the ₹10,000 note
C. Demonetisation of the ₹10,000 note in 1978
D. Demonetisation of the ₹10,000 note in 1946
accepted.x: The ₹10,000 note was introduced in 1936, demonetised in 1946, reintroduced in 1954 and demonetised again in 1978.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two intervening events.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The power to demonetise bank notes under the Reserve Bank of India Act is exercised under:
accepted.x: Section 26(2) of the RBI Act provides the power relating to demonetisation of bank notes.
accepted.tq: Test the precise statutory provision instead of the broader subject of currency issue.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the denominations withdrawn from circulation during the 2016 demonetisation?
accepted.x: On 8 November 2016, ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes were demonetised.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between denominations associated with different demonetisation episodes.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court upheld the 2016 demonetisation decision in 2023 by a majority of:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court upheld the 2016 demonetisation by a 4:1 majority in 2023.
accepted.tq: Recall the judicial majority, not merely the year of the judgment.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the ₹2,000 note is correct?
o: It was never declared legal tender by the Reserve Bank of India
It was withdrawn from circulation in November 2016 and remains legal tender only for banks
It was demonetised in May 2023 and ceased to be legal tender immediately
It was withdrawn from circulation in May 2023 but continues to be legal tender
accepted.x: The ₹2,000 note was withdrawn from circulation in May 2023 but continues to have legal-tender status.
accepted.tq: Separate withdrawal from circulation from cancellation of legal-tender status.
accepted.sec: Currency management - issuer, reserve backing, denomination, withdrawal, demonetisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (RBI regional representation) — List-II (Location)
a. North — New Delhi
a. South — Chennai
c. East — Kolkata
d. West — Mumbai
accepted.x: The four regional representations are North–New Delhi, South–Chennai, East–Kolkata and West–Mumbai.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure regional pair and verify the remaining locations.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Reserve Bank Staff College and the College of Agricultural Banking are located at, respectively:
accepted.x: The Reserve Bank Staff College is at Chennai, while the College of Agricultural Banking is at Pune.
accepted.tq: Test the location pair of specialised RBI training institutions.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an autonomous institute associated with the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research
Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology
accepted.x: NIBM, IGIDR and IDRBT are autonomous institutes. The Reserve Bank Staff College is a training college, not an autonomous institute in this classification.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring institutional category.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tarapore Committee was primarily associated with a roadmap for:
o: Transfer of RBI surplus to the Government
accepted.x: The Tarapore Committees, constituted in 1997 and 2006, examined the roadmap to capital account convertibility.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive policy objective.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bimal Jalan Committee — Economic Capital Framework
2. Nachiket Mor Committee — Differentiated banks
3. Inter-disciplinary Standing Committee — Cyber security
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Bimal Jalan Committee dealt with the Economic Capital Framework and surplus transfer, the Nachiket Mor Committee with differentiated banks, and the Inter-disciplinary Standing Committee with cyber security.
accepted.tq: Match each committee with its specialised policy area.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nachiket Mor Committee was constituted in 2013 and is associated with recommendations concerning:
o: Small finance banks and payments banks
accepted.x: The Nachiket Mor Committee, constituted in 2013, examined differentiated banks, including small finance banks and payments banks.
accepted.tq: Use the year and distinctive institutional reform as confirmation clues.
accepted.sec: RBI offices and committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Governor and Deputy Governors of the Reserve Bank of India are appointed by the:
o: President of India on the recommendation of Parliament
Central Board of the RBI independently
accepted.x: The Governor and Deputy Governors are appointed by the Government of India; the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approves the appointments.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ test to an appointment power.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the tenure provisions relating to the Governor and Deputy Governors of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Their tenure cannot exceed five years
A fixed tenure of exactly four years applies to all of them
They hold office for six years without reappointment
Their tenure is determined only by the Central Board
accepted.x: The Governor and Deputy Governors are appointed for a tenure of not more than five years.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a maximum tenure from a mandatory fixed tenure.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India consists of:
o: 15 members, with directors appointed for four years
11 members, with directors appointed for five years
25 members, with directors appointed for six years
21 members, with directors appointed for four years
accepted.x: The Central Board has 21 members, and its directors hold office for four years. They are appointed by the Government of India under the RBI Act.
accepted.tq: Combine the composition figure with the tenure figure to avoid partial matching.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly describes the usual composition of the four Deputy Governors of the Reserve Bank of India?

1. Two from the RBI ranks
2. One commercial banker
3. One economist associated with monetary policy
4. Two representatives of State Governments
accepted.x: The four Deputy Governors comprise two from within the RBI, one commercial banker and one economist who heads monetary policy. State Government representatives are not part of this stated composition.
accepted.tq: Reject the swapped membership inserted into an otherwise familiar composition.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
accepted.x: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and served from 1935 to 1937.
accepted.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the earliest tenure in the list.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: C. D. Deshmukh is associated with which of the following distinctions?
o: First Indian Governor of the RBI
First Deputy Governor from the commercial banking sector
accepted.x: C. D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and served from 1943 to 1949.
accepted.tq: Distinguish ‘first Governor’ from ‘first Indian Governor’.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Sir Osborne Smith is correct?
o: He was the first Governor of the RBI and signed no Indian note
He introduced the Minimum Reserve System in 1956
He was the first Indian Governor of the RBI and signed the first Indian banknote
He was the Governor during the 2016 demonetisation
accepted.x: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI from 1935 to 1937 and signed no Indian note because King Edward VIII had abdicated.
accepted.tq: Combine the office-holder fact with the specific exception about note signing.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rohit Jain was appointed as a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in May 2026, replacing:
accepted.x: Rohit Jain was appointed in May 2026 for a three-year term, replacing T. Rabi Sankar.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between current office-holders and the person replaced.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the Reserve Bank of India’s local boards?

List-I (Board) — List-II (Location)
a. North — New Delhi
b. South — Chennai
c. East — Kolkata
d. West — Mumbai
accepted.x: The local boards are located in New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata and Mumbai for the North, South, East and West regions respectively.
accepted.tq: Match geographical direction with the corresponding local-board headquarters.
accepted.sec: RBI governance - Governor, Central Board, Deputy Governors, Governors, accounting year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, which of the following is NOT a regulatory area associated with banking supervision?
o: Determining the constitutional composition of Parliament
accepted.x: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 covers licensing, branch opening, management, amalgamation, cash reserve and liquidity requirements, audit and inspection. It does not determine Parliament’s composition.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional function among banking-regulatory powers.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: Payments banks are licensed under which provision of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949?
accepted.x: Payments banks are licensed under Section 22(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific licensing provision and reject provisions belonging to other regulatory subjects.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: Non-Banking Financial Companies are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India under which chapter of the RBI Act?
accepted.x: NBFCs are regulated under Chapter IIIB of the Reserve Bank of India Act.
accepted.tq: Test the exact chapter number, a common statutory-provision trap.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS) 2026, effective from 1 July 2026, is based on which principle?
accepted.x: RB-IOS 2026 follows the principle of “One Nation, One Ombudsman” and covers banks, RRBs, UCBs, NBFCs and payment operators.
accepted.tq: Identify the official slogan and distinguish it from neighbouring regulatory formulations.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following institutions is covered by the Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026 along with banks, RRBs, UCBs, NBFCs and payment operators?
o: All of the institutions listed in the question itself
Only cooperative societies not engaged in banking
accepted.x: RB-IOS 2026 covers banks, Regional Rural Banks, Urban Cooperative Banks, NBFCs and payment operators. The option reflects the complete stated coverage; it does not extend only to insurers or stock exchanges.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated scope of a regulatory scheme to identify the complete coverage group.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the treatment of unclaimed deposits under the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund?
o: Only deposits of exactly ten years are transferred and no claim is thereafter possible
The Fund applies exclusively to foreign-currency deposits
Deposits unclaimed for ten or more years are transferred, but the depositor’s right survives
Deposits unclaimed for less than one year are transferred and the depositor’s right ends
accepted.x: Under Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, unclaimed deposits of ten or more years are transferred to the DEA Fund, but the depositor’s right to claim survives.
accepted.tq: Separate transfer to the Fund from extinguishment of the depositor’s claim.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Depositor Education and Awareness Fund was established in:
accepted.x: The DEA Fund was established in 2014 under Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
accepted.tq: Use the year linked to the statutory provision rather than the year of a later banking reform.
accepted.sec: Regulatory functions - BR Act 1949, NBFC supervision  [other exams]
